messages:
erin: heads-up — got a report that a large org apply produced a 2min tail in route reconciliation. not a full outage but visible customer pain. logs below.

erin: ```
[2026-03-23T13:02:01Z] apply-run: id=APPLY-PI-114 user=marta scope=org:420 flags=312
[2026-03-23T13:02:03Z] orchestrator: planned_batches=26 estimated_tasks=3120
[2026-03-23T13:02:05Z] router-pool-us-central: inflight=1120 capacity=1200 queue_depth=980
[2026-03-23T13:02:07Z] router-pool-us-central: tail_latency_p95=320ms baseline=80ms
[2026-03-23T13:02:09Z] apply-run: degraded_tail_latency=true paused=false
```

erin: summary: tail lat increase, not total throughput failure. appears correlated with many small routes that induce hot-path CPU on routers.

li: oh interesting — this is different from the queue_depth-only incidents. tail latency implies latency SLOs we care about. did preview show anything?

marta: we ran preview but it only returned "risk: low" because it used simple route_count heuristics. missed hotspot because this org has many short-lived ephemeral routes.

vijay: proposal: introduce a per-scope "apply_budget" concept and a sequence-aware orchestrator. instead of only parallelism/window, we allocate budget tokens per tenant/org that limit total concurrent route-invalidations targeting a single router shard. token burn rate is route-sensitive (weight routes by expected recon cost).

li: can you expand "recon cost"?

vijay: recon cost = expected downstream work for a route change: estimate from historical traces (avg kv ops, fanout size), or fallback to a route-type default. store lightweight route profiles in telemetry aggregator. weigh heavy routes higher so budgets protect routers from many cheap vs few expensive ops.

sre-bot: suggestion: add metrics: apply.preflight.estimated_tail_latency, apply.budget.tokens_used, apply.budget.estimated_peak.

erin: I like budgets. how would preview surface this?

vijay: estimator endpoint POST /v1/apply/estimate should accept {scope, parallelism, budget_mode=[legacy|budgeted]} and return {estimated_peak, estimated_tail_ms, budget_tokens_required, suggested_budget_tokens}. The console preview UI can show a small heatmap: per-pool peak and predicted tail latency with color bands.

marta: UX: heatmap on preview modal sounds great. show per-pool suggested_budget_tokens and a one-click "apply with safe budget" that rewrites apply_controls to include budget_tokens and sequence=true. Also an "expedite" checkbox for admins that consumes an override token and requires audit justification.

li: runtime changes: orchestrator will implement token-bucket per-shard derived from pool_capacity and route-profile weights. if budget_tokens_required > tenant_quota -> recommend splitting apply or lowering parallelism. Also sequence=true will cause orchestrator to order batches by route-weight (heavy-first or heavy-last?) — we should decide.

vijay: heavy-first helps free caches earlier for subsequent small changes, but might spike early. heavy-last smooths immediate load. default heavy-last for safety. expose apply_controls.sequence_preference=[heavy_first|heavy_last|balanced].

erin: audit/compliance: any override or expedite must create audit log and increment a tenant_override metric. enterprises can disable expedite.

marta: telemetry: emit apply.preflight.heatmap (small JSON encoded string), apply.budget.suggested_tokens, apply.override.count. Also add a preview flag so dry-run includes tail latency estimate.

li: question: how expensive will estimator be? we need it to be cheap and cacheable.

vijay: estimator will be approximate: use cached route profiles per tenant shard (TTL 1h) + pool capacity snapshot. worst-case do a conservative upper bound. POST /v1/apply/estimate should be O(#shards) cheap.

erin: ops runbook: if estimated_tail_ms > 2x baseline or budget_tokens_required > 0.8 * tenant_budget then auto-pause and suggest safe defaults. default auto-pause on for non-admins.

marta: implementation plan: 
1) add route-profile sampler and store aggregated weights (vijay)
2) estimator endpoint + heatmap telemetry (li)
3) orchestrator token-bucket + sequence handling (erin)
4) console heatmap + safe apply button + expedite flow (marta)

marta: proposed owners & ETA: vijay prototype route-profiles (3d), li adds estimator (+heatmap) (4d), erin implements budget gating (5d), marta consoles UI + copy (6d).

vijay: dev question  should tenant_budget be configurable per-tenant? we should allow org-level policies to tune budgets, but also have a sane global default derived from pool capacity.

li: yes configurable. console org settings: default_budget_tokens and override controls. API should accept apply_controls.budget_tokens and apply_controls.sequence_preference.

erin: one more ops detail: add a temporary "preflight-accept" token we can give to SRE to run an apply that bypasses budget for emergency fixes; these tokens expire and are recorded.

marta: fine, but require two-person approval for preflight-accept tokens in prod.

sre-bot: incident created: APPLY-PI-114 review ticket INF-8711 linked.

erin: action items:
- vijay: route-profile prototype + metrics (due 2026-03-26)
- li: estimator endpoint + heatmap telemetry + tests (due 2026-03-27)
- erin: orchestrator budget gating + sequence handling + runbook (due 2026-03-29)
- marta: console heatmap + safe-apply + expedite UI (due 2026-03-30)

marta: creating ticket INF-8711 and linking incident. leaving thread open for progress posts. :eyes:
